title: Then go out and seek
hookLine: when the prayer is done, disperse and seek Allah's bounty (62:10)

lines: SHOES FROM THE PILE BY THE DOOR.
cards: The Friday prayer ends. People stand, shake hands, find their shoes in the pile by the door. Within ten minutes the shutters are back up, the taxis are moving, the office towers are filling again.
A holy day might sound like a day off, set apart from work and money. The very next verse of Surah Al-Jumu'ah doesn't tell people to stay. It sends them out the door.

teach.b: Verse ten. Pickthall: "And when the prayer is ended, then disperse in the land and seek of Allah's bounty, and remember Allah much, that ye may be successful." Three verbs.
Fantashiru, disperse, spread out through the land. Wabtaghu, seek, from God's bounty, fadl, which commentators read here as earning a living.
And udhkuru, remember God much. Commentators read the command to go out as a permission, not an obligation: the previous verse's restriction is lifted. Still, the order is telling.
Friday here isn't a day off. It's a day with one hour carved out for gathering, then work resumes, with remembrance carried into it. Then verse eleven tells a story against the community itself.
One Friday, while the Prophet ﷺ was giving the sermon, a trade caravan arrived in Medina. People slipped out to it and left him standing. Bukhari and Muslim report that only twelve men remained.

The verse records it plainly, and adds: what is with God is better than amusement and trade, and God is the best of providers. So verses nine to eleven make a little circle. Leave trade for the prayer.
After the prayer, go seek a living. But never leave the prayer for the trade.

teach.h: REMEMBER GOD MUCH, OUT IN THE MARKET.
teach.b: Remembrance at the center, work around it, and the word much: remember God much, out in the market too.

how: After the Friday prayer, many Muslims return to work or business; Friday is a day of congregation rather than a required day of rest, though some countries include it in the weekend.

games.q: the Prophet is giving the Friday sermon. word comes that a trade caravan has arrived in town. what do many of the people do?
o: slip out to the caravan, leaving him standing.
games.why: many left; only twelve remained. verse eleven records it and says what is with God is better than amusement and trade.

practice: If you pray, think of your next prayer and the work that follows it; if you don't, let this quiet be your pause.
Picture the very next task waiting for you, and see yourself starting it calmly, carrying a little of this quiet into it, doing it carefully, as if it counted.

wordCard.voice: Fadl: God's bounty, what Surah Al-Jumu'ah tells believers to go out and seek once the Friday prayer ends. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: then disperse in the land. Spoken right after the Friday prayer ends.

carryVoice: Your line: pray, then work. Remembrance travels with you into the market. Day six hundred twenty-seven.
